es.summary: La ezetimiba es un inhibidor de la absorción intestinal de colesterol que reduce los niveles de LDL‑C.
key_points: Inhibe el transportador NPC1L1 en el intestino delgado.
Se usa para hipercolesterolemia, solo o con estatinas.
No requiere ajuste de dosis en insuficiencia renal leve.
Monitorear enzimas hepáticas y signos de miopatía.
Se administra una vez al día, con o sin alimentos.

mechanism: Bloquea NPC1L1, impidiendo la incorporación de colesterol dietético y biliar en los enterocitos.
Disminuye la cantidad de colesterol que llega al hígado.
El hígado aumenta la captación de LDL de la sangre, reduciendo el LDL‑C.
indications: Hipercolesterolemia primaria o secundaria cuando la estatina no alcanza la meta.
Pacientes que no toleran dosis altas de estatinas.
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad conocida a la ezetimiba o a sus excipientes.
Embarazo y lactancia (categoría X en Costa Rica).
adverse_effects: Mialgia o rabdomiólisis cuando se combina con estatinas (serio).
interactions: Ciclosporina: eleva niveles plasmáticos de ezetimiba.
Secuestrantes de ácidos biliares: reducen absorción de ezetimiba.
Anticoagulantes: monitorizar INR por posible alteración del metabolismo hepático.
nursing_care: Obtener perfil lipídico y pruebas de función hepática antes de iniciar.
Evaluar dolor muscular, debilidad o cambios en la orina durante el tratamiento.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si ALT/AST >3× límite superior normal.
Verificar que el paciente tome la tableta completa con agua, sin masticar.
Revisar lista de medicamentos para detectar interacciones potenciales.
patient_teaching: Tomar una tableta al día, con o sin alimentos.
Mantener dieta baja en grasas y colesterol según indicaciones del nutricionista.
Reportar cualquier dolor muscular, debilidad o coloración oscura de la orina.
Informar al médico sobre cualquier nuevo medicamento, incluido suplementos herbales.

outcomes: Control de lípidos dentro del rango objetivo en 3 meses.
Enzimas hepáticas (ALT, AST) dentro de límites normales durante el tratamiento.

interventions.action: Obtener perfil lipídico basal y repetir cada 8‑12 semanas.
interventions.rationale: Permite evaluar la efectividad del tratamiento.

interventions.action: Monitorear pruebas de función hepática antes y durante el uso.
Evaluar dolor muscular y fuerza cada visita.
interventions.rationale: Identifica signos de miopatía o rabdomiólisis.

interventions.action: Revisar lista de medicamentos para interacciones con estatinas y ciclosporina.
Educar al paciente sobre signos de lesión hepática y muscular.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección precoz y la intervención oportuna.

interventions.action: Notificar al médico si ALT/AST >3× límite superior normal o si aparecen síntomas musculares.
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar o suspender el tratamiento rápidamente.

en.summary: Ezetimibe is an intestinal cholesterol absorption inhibitor that reduces LDL‑C levels.
key_points: Inhibits the NPC1L1 transporter in the small intestine.
Used for hypercholesterolemia, alone or with statins.
No dose adjustment needed in mild renal impairment.
Monitor liver enzymes and signs of myopathy.
Administer once daily, with or without food.

mechanism: Blocks NPC1L1, preventing incorporation of dietary and biliary cholesterol into enterocytes.
Reduces the amount of cholesterol reaching the liver.
The liver increases uptake of LDL from the blood, lowering LDL‑C.
indications: Primary or secondary hypercholesterolemia when statin therapy does not reach target.
Patients who cannot tolerate high-dose statins.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to ezetimibe or its excipients.
Pregnancy and lactation (Category X in Costa Rica).
adverse_effects: Myalgia or rhabdomyolysis when combined with statins (serious).
interactions: Cyclosporine: raises plasma levels of ezetimibe.
Bile acid sequestrants: reduce absorption of ezetimibe.
Anticoagulants: monitor INR due to possible hepatic metabolism changes.
nursing_care: Obtain lipid profile and liver function tests before starting.
Assess for muscle pain, weakness, or changes in urine during treatment.
Hold dose and notify provider if ALT/AST >3× upper limit of normal.
Ensure patient takes the tablet whole with water, not chewed.
Review medication list for potential interactions.
patient_teaching: Take one tablet daily, with or without food.
Maintain a low‑fat, low‑cholesterol diet as directed by the dietitian.
Report any muscle pain, weakness, or dark urine color.
Inform provider of any new medications, including herbal supplements.

outcomes: Lipid control within target range in 3 months.
Liver enzymes (ALT, AST) within normal limits during treatment.

interventions.action: Obtain baseline lipid profile and repeat every 8‑12 weeks.
Monitor liver function tests before and during use.
Assess muscle pain and strength at each visit.
interventions.rationale: Identifies signs of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis.

interventions.action: Review medication list for interactions with statins and cyclosporine.
Educate patient on signs of hepatic and muscular injury.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection and timely intervention.

interventions.action: Notify provider if ALT/AST >3× upper limit of normal or if muscular symptoms appear.
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid adjustment or discontinuation of therapy.

summary.0.quote: Ezetimibe is a cholesterol absorption inhibitor.

key_points.0.quote: It works by inhibiting the cholesterol transporter called Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1).

sections.indications.1.quote: Indications Primary hypercholesterolemia Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia Homozygous sitosterolemia

sections.contraindications.0.quote: Ezetimibe should not be used in clients with active liver disease or unexplained elevations in transaminase levels, those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, or those with hypersensitivity to the drug or any of its product components.

sections.contraindications.1.quote: Ezetimibe should not be used in clients with active liver disease or unexplained elevations in transaminase levels, those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, or those with hypersensitivity to the drug or any of its product components.

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: The most significant adverse events associated with ezetimibe are liver enzyme abnormalities, myopathy, and rhabdomyolysis, especially when the drug is combined with statin medications.
